property_tests.description: Calling PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with the same non-empty permissions array twice produces the same PATResponse as calling it once.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample a valid token_id from the pats table and a non-empty subset of the 7 registered permissions (up to 7 elements, randomly chosen). Run 50 iterations with different permission subsets.
property_tests.invariant_check: resp1 = PUT(tokenID, perms); resp2 = PUT(tokenID, perms); assert resp1.body.permissions == resp2.body.permissions; assert resp1.body.revoked_at == resp2.body.revoked_at

property_tests.description: After any sequence of PATCH add requests with overlapping permissions, the permissions array in the pats table never contains duplicate entries.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample a valid token_id and generate sequences of 1-10 PATCH requests each with a random non-empty subset of the 7 registered permissions. Run 100 iterations.
property_tests.invariant_check: for each sequence of PATCH requests: execute all requests; dbPerms = queryDB("SELECT permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", tokenID); parsed = parseJSON(dbPerms); assert len(parsed) == len(set(parsed))

property_tests.description: Calling DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with the same permissions array twice produces the same PATResponse as calling it once.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample a valid non-revoked token_id with at least 2 permissions and a non-empty subset of those permissions to remove. Run 50 iterations.
property_tests.invariant_check: resp1 = DELETE(tokenID, perms); resp2 = DELETE(tokenID, perms); assert resp1.body.permissions == resp2.body.permissions; assert resp1.body.revoked_at == resp2.body.revoked_at

property_tests.description: For any replace or remove operation on a non-revoked, non-expired token, revoked_at is set if and only if the resulting permissions array is empty.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample a valid non-revoked, non-expired token_id and a random permissions array (including empty for PUT). For DELETE, sample a random subset of the token's current permissions. Run 100 iterations covering both PUT and DELETE.
property_tests.invariant_check: resp = operation(tokenID, perms); resultingPerms = resp.body.permissions; if len(resultingPerms) == 0: assert resp.body.revoked_at != null; else: assert resp.body.revoked_at == null

property_tests.description: For any permission modification request with a token_id belonging to a different user, the handler returns HTTP 404 and makes no changes to the pats table.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample pairs of (userA_token, userB_token_id) where userA is the authenticated caller and userB_token_id belongs to a different user. Try all three HTTP methods (PUT, PATCH, DELETE). Run 30 iterations per method.
property_tests.invariant_check: permsBefore = queryDB("SELECT permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", userBTokenID); resp = sendRequest(method, "/user/tokens/"+userBTokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(userAPAT), body({permissions:["users:read"]})); assert resp.status == 404; permsAfter = queryDB("SELECT permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", userBTokenID); assert permsBefore == permsAfter

property_tests.description: For any PAT-authenticated caller and any permission not held by the caller's PAT, a replace or add request that would grant that permission is rejected with HTTP 403.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample a caller PAT with a random subset of the 7 permissions (always including tokens:write). Sample a target permission not in the caller's set. Try both PUT and PATCH. Run 50 iterations.
property_tests.invariant_check: resp = sendRequest(method, "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(callerPAT), body({permissions:[escalatingPerm]})); assert resp.status == 403; assert resp.body.error == "cannot grant permission: "+escalatingPerm

property_tests.description: For any token with non-null revoked_at or with expires_at in the past, all three permission modification endpoints return HTTP 400 and make no changes to the pats table.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample tokens in two states: (a) revoked_at non-null, (b) expires_at in the past. Try all three HTTP methods with valid permission arrays. Run 30 iterations per state per method.
property_tests.invariant_check: permsBefore = queryDB("SELECT permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", tokenID); resp = sendRequest(method, "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(validPAT), body({permissions:["users:read"]})); assert resp.status == 400; permsAfter = queryDB("SELECT permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", tokenID); assert permsBefore == permsAfter

property_tests.description: After any successful replace or add operation, every permission string in the pats.permissions JSON array is registered in the PermissionRegistry and contains exactly one colon.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample a valid token_id and a random non-empty subset of the 7 registered permissions. Try both PUT and PATCH. Run 100 iterations.
property_tests.invariant_check: resp = sendRequest(method, "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(apiKey), body({permissions:perms})); assert resp.status == 200; dbPerms = parseJSON(queryDB("SELECT permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", tokenID)); for p in dbPerms: assert count(p, ':') == 1; assert registry.IsRegistered(p) == true

property_tests.description: Every call to NewPermissionRegistry() returns a registry containing exactly 7 built-in permissions including tokens:write.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Call NewPermissionRegistry() 20 times in independent goroutines to verify no race conditions or non-determinism in the count.
property_tests.invariant_check: for i in range(20): registry = NewPermissionRegistry(); assert len(registry.All()) == 7; assert registry.IsRegistered("tokens:write") == true

Target PAT exists
Caller has tokens:write permission
Echo test server running with auth middleware
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: resp = sendRequest("PUT", "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(validPAT), body({permissions:["users:read:extra"]})); assert resp.status == 400; assert resp.body.error == "invalid permission format: users:read:extra"

edge_case_tests.description: A PAT caller replacing their own token's permissions with a subset of their own permissions is allowed without triggering the escalation guard.
preconditions: SQLite in-memory database initialized with pats table
Caller PAT has permissions ["tokens:write", "users:read", "orgs:read"]
Target PAT is the same token as the caller's PAT (self-modification)
Echo test server running with auth middleware

input.auth: Bearer own PAT with tokens:write, users:read, orgs:read

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: resp = sendRequest("PUT", "/user/tokens/"+ownTokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(ownPAT), body({permissions:["users:read"]})); assert resp.status == 200; assert resp.body.permissions == ["users:read"]

edge_case_tests.description: A PAT caller attempting to add a permission to a token that the caller's own PAT does not hold is rejected with HTTP 403.
preconditions: SQLite in-memory database initialized with pats table
Caller PAT has permissions ["tokens:write", "users:read"]
Target PAT exists with permissions ["users:read"]
Echo test server running with auth middleware

input.auth: Bearer PAT with tokens:write and users:read

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: resp = sendRequest("PUT", "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(callerPAT), body({permissions:["tokens:manage"]})); assert resp.status == 403; assert resp.body.error == "cannot grant permission: tokens:manage"

edge_case_tests.description: A database UPDATE failure during replace rolls back the transaction and returns HTTP 500 with 'internal server error'.
preconditions: Echo test server running with auth middleware
Database is configured to fail on UPDATE queries (mock/stub)
Target PAT exists and passes all guards
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: injectDBError(updateFails=true); resp = sendRequest("PUT", "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(validPAT), body({permissions:["users:read"]})); assert resp.status == 500; assert resp.body.error == "internal server error"

edge_case_tests.description: Concurrent replace requests on the same token both complete with HTTP 200; the final state reflects the last committed write (last-write-wins).
preconditions: SQLite in-memory database initialized with pats table
Target PAT exists with permissions ["users:read"]
Two goroutines ready to send concurrent PUT requests
Echo test server running with auth middleware
edge_case_tests.input: two concurrent PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions requests with different permissions arrays
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: results = concurrentRequests([PUT(tokenID, ["users:read"]), PUT(tokenID, ["orgs:read"])]); assert all(r.status == 200 for r in results); finalPerms = getTokenPermissions(tokenID); assert finalPerms == ["users:read"] OR finalPerms == ["orgs:read"]

edge_case_tests.description: If the auto-revocation UPDATE fails within db.WithTx, the entire transaction is rolled back and HTTP 500 is returned; token state is unchanged.
preconditions: Echo test server running with auth middleware
Database is configured to fail on the second UPDATE within a transaction (mock/stub)
Target PAT exists with permissions ["users:read"]
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: injectDBError(secondUpdateFails=true); resp = sendRequest("PUT", "/user/tokens/"+tokenID+"/permissions", authHeader(validPAT), body({permissions:[]})); assert resp.status == 500; assert resp.body.error == "internal server error"; dbRow = queryDB("SELECT revoked_at, permissions FROM pats WHERE id = ?", tokenID); assert dbRow.revoked_at == null; assert dbRow.permissions == '["users:read"]'

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for the replace PAT permissions happy path: a PAT caller with tokens:write replaces a token's permissions and receives HTTP 200 with updated PATResponse.
smoke_tests.trigger: Send PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with Authorization: Bearer <PAT with tokens:write> and body {permissions: ["users:read", "orgs:read"]}
expected_effects: HTTP 200 response with PATResponse JSON body
PATResponse.permissions equals ["users:read", "orgs:read"]
PATResponse.revoked_at is null
pats table row for token_id has permissions column updated to '["users:read","orgs:read"]'
pats table row revoked_at remains NULL

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for replace with empty array triggering auto-revocation: PUT with [] results in HTTP 200 with revoked_at set in the response and database.
smoke_tests.trigger: Send PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with Authorization: Bearer <PAT with tokens:write> and body {permissions: []}
expected_effects: HTTP 200 response with PATResponse JSON body
PATResponse.permissions equals []
PATResponse.revoked_at is non-null and a valid UTC timestamp
pats table row for token_id has permissions column set to '[]'
pats table row revoked_at is non-null

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for the add permissions happy path: a PAT caller with tokens:write adds a new permission and receives HTTP 200 with merged permissions.
smoke_tests.trigger: Send PATCH /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with Authorization: Bearer <PAT with tokens:write and orgs:write> and body {permissions: ["orgs:write"]}
expected_effects: HTTP 200 response with PATResponse JSON body
PATResponse.permissions contains both the original permission and orgs:write
PATResponse.revoked_at is null
pats table row permissions column contains the merged set with no duplicates

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for remove all permissions triggering auto-revocation: DELETE removes the last permission, resulting in HTTP 200 with revoked_at set.
smoke_tests.trigger: Send DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with Authorization: Bearer <PAT with tokens:write> and body {permissions: ["users:read"]} where users:read is the only permission on the target token
expected_effects: HTTP 200 response with PATResponse JSON body
PATResponse.permissions equals []
PATResponse.revoked_at is non-null and a valid UTC timestamp
pats table row for token_id has permissions column set to '[]'
pats table row revoked_at is non-null

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for the akc tokens replace CLI command: the CLI parses permissions, sends PUT via DoRequest, prints PATResponse JSON to stdout, and prints revocation warning to stderr if auto-revoked.
expected_effects: CLI exits with code 0
stdout contains valid PATResponse JSON with permissions ["users:read","orgs:read"]
stderr is empty (no revocation, since permissions are non-empty)
pats table row permissions column updated to '["users:read","orgs:read"]'

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for the full PAT permission lifecycle: create → add → replace → remove, verifying state at each step and confirming auto-revocation at the end.
smoke_tests.trigger: Execute the full lifecycle sequence: POST /user/tokens (create with users:read), PATCH (add orgs:read), PUT (replace with orgs:write), DELETE (remove orgs:write → auto-revoke)
expected_effects: After create: PATResponse.permissions == ["users:read"], revoked_at == null
After add: PATResponse.permissions == ["users:read", "orgs:read"], revoked_at == null
After replace: PATResponse.permissions == ["orgs:write"], revoked_at == null
After remove: PATResponse.permissions == [], revoked_at is non-null
pats table row for token_id has revoked_at set after the final DELETE
